content.text:
Compose starts Vite in `/app/frontend` and bind-mounts `./frontend` there ([compose.yaml](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-posthog-pr/compose.yaml:14), [Dockerfile.dev](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-posthog-pr/frontend/Dockerfile.dev:3)). SvelteKit loads frontend environment values and exposes the two variables declared public in [env.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-posthog-pr/frontend/src/env.ts:9). Client `init()` reads them and calls `posthog.init()`. Missing values throw during development ([hooks.client.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-posthog-pr/frontend/src/hooks.client.ts:9)).

The missing connection is configuration. Compose forwards only API origin and polling settings, with no `env_file` ([compose.yaml](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-posthog-pr/compose.yaml:8)). Root `.env` values therefore do not automatically reach the frontend container. The frontend example supplies placeholders, but `.env.example` is not an active environment file ([frontend/.env.example](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-posthog-pr/frontend/.env.example:1)).

The smallest local fix is to copy `frontend/.env.example` to ignored `frontend/.env`, populate the project token, and restart frontend. The bind mount makes that file available to Vite without rebuilding the image. Existing `frontend/.gitignore` already excludes it.

If the requested deliverable must change tracked Compose configuration, add explicit `PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` interpolation entries under the frontend `environment`, then document their root `.env` setup. This matches Compose’s existing explicit environment mapping. Keep the client initialization unchanged.
